text: Texas elected gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa, who supports a data center moratorium. The state accounts for approximately 27% of planned U.S. data center capacity. SpaceX fell 7%, CoreWeave 7%, Iren 6%, Nebius 3%, and Oracle 4.3%, while several major hyperscalers gained.

meta.note: The proposed moratorium is not enacted; reported capacity shares refer to planned projects.

text: McDonald's reported Q3 revenue of $7.16 billion (+1% YoY), adjusted EPS of $3.57, and net income of $2.49 billion. Global same-store sales rose 1.5%, while U.S. sales fell 0.2% amid lower traffic. International licensed markets grew 4.2%; operated markets rose 1.4%.

meta.note: U.S. traffic declined; the reported 0.2% decrease measures same-store sales rather than visit counts.

text: ADP reported 86,000 private jobs added in October, matching revised September figures. Trade, transportation and utilities gained 39,000; education and health added 28,000. Professional and business services lost 27,000. Job-changer base pay rose 4.8% annually versus 3% for job-stayers.

meta.note: ADP estimates cover private employment and are distinct from the pending BLS payroll report.

text: CVS announced plans to separate its roughly 9,000 retail pharmacies from its insurance, PBM, and healthcare services operations by H1 2028. Both entities would be publicly traded, with existing shareholders retaining stakes in each. Q3 revenue reached $108.40 billion; shares fell approximately 10%.

meta.note: Separation remains prospective; existing integrated operations have not yet been divided.

text: WTI crude fell nearly 9% to $87.59 per barrel; Brent declined over 9% to $93.91. Oil futures were down more than 14% for the week. U.S. officials expressed openness to diplomacy with Iran, while military escalation remained unresolved. Democrats secured congressional majorities.

meta.note: Market repricing is observable; the relative influence of electoral results and diplomatic signals remains undetermined.
